Pleased To Allow The Claim Petition By Granting The
Relief As Prayed For By The Appellant, In The Interest
Of Justice And Equity.
 This Appeal Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Aggrieved by the dismissal of MVC No.128/2006 dated 30.07.2015, the claimants are before this Court.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.
2. It is the case of the claimants that on 16.10.2005 one Vishwanath Appannappa Dalawai was traveling on a motorcycle as pillion rider.

One Sangappa Kolar was riding the said motorcycle, at about 7.30 a.m. NC: 2024:KHC-K:544 due to the rash and negligent riding of the said motorcycle,
both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained severe grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was taken to the hospital, Vijaypur and later he was shifted to Bengaluru Hospital.
On 23.10.2005 he succumbed to the said injuries, the claimants have spent huge amount for the treatment.
On behalf of the claimants, PW1 and PW2 i.e. the parents of the deceased were examined, Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 were marked.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P3 are the police documents, Ex.P4 is the post mortem report and Ex.P5 the statement of one Basappa on 23.10.2005 and other documents are marked as Ex.P5(a) to Ex.P8.
On behalf of respondents RW1 and RW2 were examined and they have marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R18.
Ex.R8 to Ex.R17 are the depositions of the witnesses before the criminal Court where he has turned hostile.
Ex.R18 is the case sheet of the deceased.
The Court below had dismissed the claim petition on the ground that Ex.R8 discloses that the history is reported as RTA fall from bike on his own.
The Court has also observed that when accident had taken place on NC: 2024:KHC-K:544 15.10.2005 the complaint was lodged on 14.02.2005.

The deceased died on 23.10.2005, even after that no Appannappa S/O Ramswami Dalawai vs Virupaxappa S/O Basappa Kinagi on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123843579/
2 complaint was lodged and it was lodged after two months.

sentences.text: The Court below had observed that all the documents were produced by the insurance company and no positive evidence is adduced by the petitioner.
The deposition of PW1 and PW2 is that deceased was a pillion rider and he sustained injuries and succumbed to the same.
His deposition before the Court is contrary to the depositions before the Criminal Court where they turned hostile.
The Court below has held that the story put forth by the claimants is not trustworthy and had dismissed the claim petition.
3. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that he was admitted in the hospital on 06.10.2005 immediately on the same day it is mentioned as RTA.
It is the duty of the hospital authority to intimate the same to the police their latches cannot be attributed to the claimant.
It is submitted that deceased died on NC: 2024:KHC-K:544 23.10.2005 on the same day one eye witness has given a statement before the police.
The police have not taken any action, it cannot be termed as a delay and in fact the earliest point of time it was brought to the notice of the police.
Learned counsel submits that all the circumstances show that he is a pillion rider and he had sustained injuries.

When he could establish that he died because of the injury sustained in the accident and the accident had happed because of the negligent on the part of the rider, the deceased pillion under is entitled for compensation and this Court and the Court below more basing on the fact that there is a delay in giving the complaint had dismissed the claim petition, which is contrary to the evidence on record.
It is submitted that in the case sheet though in the first page it is stated that it fall from bike on his own and second page it is mentioned as only fall from bike.
He submits that the Court below ought to have considered and granted the compensation.

Learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that when the accident had taken place on 16.10.2005 the family member has given a complaint on 14.12.2005 which shows that this is an after thought for the purpose of claiming the compensation, they have stated that he is a pillion rider and somebody else was driving the vehicle.

He submits that when the matter came up on 29.05.2023 before this Court considering the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant, this Court had directed the Court below to permit the petitioner to record the statement of one Basappa who is the eye witness and also the rider of the bike.
When the matter is remanded, they have not examined the rider of the bike but they have only examined the eye witness who says that he is a pillion rider.
After remand the witness has given the statement on 23.10.2005 stating that before the criminal Court he has stated that he has not seen the accident and he has no knowledge about it.
In the evidence it is stated that he along with another five people went to the place of occurrence within 10 minutes and NC: 2024:KHC-K:544 after 2-3 hours they have taken him to the hospital.
It is stated that there is no statement given whether he is a pillion rider or he is a rider of a bike.
In the cross examination it is stated that he is a pillion rider.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that he has taken two stands one before the Court below and one before this Court.

Before the criminal court he has stated that he has not seen the incident and he has no knowledge about it and in the cross examination he has stated that the deceased was the pillion rider, the said statement cannot be taken into consideration.

He submits as the tortfeasor himself is not entitled for the compensation, story is put forth to show that he is a pillion rider and he submits that the Court below has rightly dismissed the claim petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.
The accident had taken place on 15.10.2005 and the complaint was given on 14.12.2005.
As per the medical records, immediately NC: 2024:KHC-K:544 when he admitted it is stated that it is RTA self fall from the bike and another place fall from bike.
The bike do not belonged to the deceased.
He has taken the bike of first respondent and bike of first respondent is taken by whom whether the rider or the pillion rider is not known.
Then both the rider and the deceased were going on the said bike.
According to the learned counsel for the claimants some statement was given on 23.10.2005.

There is no delay in giving the information to the police, if at all there is any delay i.e. because of the latches on the part of the hospital authorities and police and it cannot be attributed to the LRs of the deceased.
The delay in giving the complaint will not be fatal to the case of the claimant, the delay has to be analyzed basing on the facts and circumstance of each case.

Coming to the facts of the case,
claimant has not even filed the extract of MLC or any other document, in fact the said discharge summary is filed by the insurance company as Ex.R8.

When he has come before the Court seeking compensation under Section 166 of M.V. Act, the burden lies on the claimant to NC:
2024:KHC-K:544 prove that the deceased died in the accident because of the involvement of the vehicle and there is negligence on the part of the rider of the vehicle.
In this case neither the owner nor the rider of the vehicle were examined by the claimants.
In these circumstances, the complaint given by the family on 14.12.2005 after long delay assume significant and such delay is definitely fatal to the case of the claimant.
The person who is said to have given statement on 23.10.2005 has come before the criminal Court and says that he has not even seen the incident and now after the remand.
It is stated that the deceased is the pillion rider.
The witnesses cannot be permitted to blow hot and cold at the same time.

He cannot take two stands on oath before a criminal court when he has categorically stated that they have not seen the incident and giving a different statement before this Court, these kind of witnesses are wholly unreliable without and their evidence cannot be believable.
In the considered opinion of this Court that the claimants failed to prove that the accident took place on 16.10.2005 and the deceased being a pillion rider had sustained the injuries.
Hence, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the well considered award passed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
